purpose: C5 (notes/008, owner's change): IonQ noise parameters from internet-published data only; no account, no API (the IonQ characterization endpoints were not called)

conventions.errors: Vendor page: 1Q error = Clifford RB error rate; 2Q error = direct randomized benchmarking (DRB) error rate; SPAM = average error of state preparation and measurement.
conventions.noise_model_doc: IonQ's published simulator noise model (Aria-class and pre-Sept-2025 Forte): depolarizing channels after each gate, K0 = sqrt(1 - 3 r1q/4) I, Ki = sqrt(r1q/4) sigma_i (1q) and K00 = sqrt(1 - 15 r2q/16) I x I, Kij = sqrt(r2q/16) sigma_i x sigma_j (2q).

forte_ent_page.title: IonQ Forte Enterprise product page (#AQ 36, 36 qubits; same specification block as Forte)

forte_paper.title: J.-S. Chen et al., Benchmarking a trapped-ion quantum computer with 30 qubits, arXiv:2308.05071v2 (Quantum, accepted 2024-10-15)

noise_doc.title: IonQ docs - Simulation with Noise Models
noise_doc.source_date: not stated; mentions the September 2025 update of the Forte model

backends_doc.title: IonQ docs - Backends (Forte 1 and Forte Enterprise 1: 36 qubits; noise-model simulators up to 29 qubits)

native_doc.title: IonQ docs - Getting started with native gates (GPi, GPi2, ZZ on Forte; MS on Aria)

value: ZZ(theta) = exp(-i pi theta Z x Z), theta in turns

p2_error.qualification: '0.4%' direct RB; paper: per-pair median 46.4e-4, 10th percentile 34.5e-4, 90th 99.6e-4, best 27.8e-4

spam_error.qualification: '0.5%' average SPAM; paper: 0.5% on each qubit

t1q.qualification: total duration of each single-qubit gate (nine pi/2 pulses, SK1 sequence)

parallelism.qualification: not published; modelled as serial gate execution (one gate at a time)

simulator_noise_model_pre_2025-09.qualification: parameters of IonQ's own depolarizing noise model for Forte 1 jobs before mid-September 2025; 'should not be directly compared to experimentally obtained error rates'

note.value: identical published numbers to Forte; one model ('ionq_forte') covers both

p2_fidelity_target.qualification: '99.9 % Target fidelity' (a design target, not a benchmark result)

other.qualification: no published 1q error, SPAM, T1/T2 or gate durations ('faster gate speeds' without numbers)

model_inputs._note: Subset used by noise_models.py. ionq_tempo is a TARGET-SPEC model: only p2 = 1 - 0.999 is published; p1, SPAM, T2 and durations are inherited from Forte (assumption, labelled in every result).
